about: Stages and timing for the supplier-review playbook. scripts/handoff.py reads this file: the stages it tracks, the outcomes each stage can record, and how long to wait between stages. The timing key and waiting outcome are the test-and-learn playbook's. Each key is explained under notes.

stages.name: review
stages.do: Score the brand against the account, add the queries it's buried on as findings, and ask the user which boost to test.

stages.name: test
stages.do: Set up an A/B test of a brand boost on the chosen query, and start it after its own yes.

skip_when.reason: the review found no query where a boost is worth testing.

stages.name: read-out
stages.do: Read the test's result. Don't stop early on a good-looking day.

skip_when.reason: the test stage was skipped, so no test is running.

stages.name: close
stages.do: End the test keeping the boost (or today's ranking), check every rule, then archive it, each step after its own yes.

skip_when.reason: no test was read out, so there is nothing to close.

stages.name: talking-points
stages.do: Re-run the review for the brand and write the supplier and co-op talking points, with the test's result.

notes.min_test_days: Days after the test stage finishes (the test started) before the read-out stage is due. The same as the test-and-learn playbook: discovery-experiment-setup recommends at least 14 days in whole weeks; use the end date agreed at setup when it's later.
notes.wait_outcomes: Outcomes that mean a stage isn't finished yet. The script records them only with status in_progress and a --not-before date to come back on, so status never shows the stage as due before then.
notes.playbooks: Each playbook's title, product and stages in order. A stage names the skill that does it, whether that skill writes, what to do, the outcomes it can record, not_before (wait this rules key's number of days after another stage is done) and skip_when (suggest skipping when another stage had one of these outcomes).
